result_text:
I changed the two mock-folder rules in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java` (lines 393–394):

- `.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` is now `.*/__mock[^/]*/.*`
- `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` is now `.*/mock[^/]*/.*`

Any folder name starting with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as test code. That covers plain `mock/`, `mock.data/`, `mock(old)/`, `mock-größe/` and `mock模拟/`, at any depth. The match stays inside one folder name because `[^/]*` can't cross a slash. Folders like `remock/` and `demo/`, and files like `mock.java` or `mockery.java`, don't match.

I didn't change the backslash handling. `SourceFileFilter.pathMatches` already tries a slash-normalised version of the path, so Windows-style paths work with the new patterns. The old folders (`mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/`, `mockStore/`) match too, since the new class is a superset of the old one.

I ran the `ScopingConventions*Test` and `Convention*Test` tests in `codeanalyzer`, which passed. I didn't add new test cases for the new folder shapes or the non-matches, and I didn't run the full module suite.
